records.source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology.leaves: Alternate, long-petioled, 3–5 palmately lobed, 10–30 cm long, cordate or sagittate base, palmate venation
morphology.flowers: Panicles; five sepals, petals absent, stamens 25–30
morphology.fruit: Five stalked follicle-like segments up to 13 cm, seeds attached to margins of opened carpels
morphology.habitat: Cultivated and spreading by seed; Fort Worth and Gillespie County escape reports

records.diagnostic: Large palmately lobed leaves and 5 open seed-bearing carpels separate from local native trees
holds: East Asian introduction; not a target native
Old flora placed under Sterculiaceae; APG modern Malvaceae ownership preserved

morphology.habit: Woody-based herb or subshrub; shrubby South Texas plant
morphology.leaves: Often cordate, velvety below, entire to irregularly toothed and sometimes shallowly lobed
morphology.flowers: Solitary in upper leaf axils; calyx lobed nearly to base, 1.4–2.4(–2.7) cm; bright red petals 1.5–3 × 0.9–2.1 cm; staminal column red, 0.9–1.4 cm, style branches 2–7 mm
morphology.fruit: Five-celled Hibiscus capsule; species capsule measurements await direct primary source crosscheck
morphology.habitat: Dry slopes, canyons, South Texas brushland; FNA range Big Bend to lower Gulf Coast

records.diagnostic: Bright red comparatively small flowers and strongly cordate leaves, distinct from large marsh Hibiscus species
holds: Not a county-certified Hays native: FNA distribution mainly near Rio Grande
No confirmed original 1999 source treatment in retrieved file

records.source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology.habit: Annual erect or ascending, glabrous to sparingly hairy
morphology.leaves: Suborbicular cordate/reniform, sometimes lobed, to 7 cm long × 12 cm wide

records.diagnostic: Very small petals and nearly round broad leaves with ten-part cheese-like schizocarp
holds: Non-native from western Eurasia/North Africa into Indian subcontinent; not Hays native

records.source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology.habit: Perennial with rigid woody-based stems, 0.4–1 m
morphology.leaves: Subcordate to broadly ovate/oblong, (18–)30–40(–55) mm, crenate-dentate, usually unlobed
morphology.hairs: 6–10-rayed often basally joined stellate hairs, resembling scales
morphology.flowers: Involucel with ovate/subcordate bractlets adnate at base of calyx; golden to pale orange-yellow petals (12–)15–16 mm long
morphology.fruits: (12–)14(–16) carpels, each mericarp (4–)5(–6) mm, median cusp 1.5–2.3 mm

records.diagnostic: Larger petals, basally joined multiple-rayed hairs and fruit tips with one long central cusp and two flattened adjacent cusps
holds: Older flora endemic Texas label not county-level BONAP confirmation

records.source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology.leaves: Ovate to lanceolate (17–)30–40(–65) mm, unlobed or rarely 3 lobes, dentate-serrate
morphology.hairs: Simple or 2–4-rayed stellate hairs, not normally basally united
morphology.flowers: Linear to narrowly spatulate involucel bractlets, pale golden/orange petals (6–)8–10(–13) mm
morphology.fruit: (9–)10–14(–15) carpels, segments (3–)3.5–4 mm with median cusp 0.2–1.2 mm and two divergent lateral cusps
morphology.habitat: Alkaline disturbed ground and weed sites

records.diagnostic: Smaller petals and 2–4-rayed hairs, shorter central fruit cusp and divergent lateral cusps versus M. aurantiacum
holds: 1999 calls pantropical weed; native-range Hays authorization not inferred

records.flora_name: Malvaviscus arboreus var. drummondii (Torr. & A.Gray) Schery
records.source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology.leaves: Cordate-orbicular 4–9 cm, about as long as wide, shallowly 3-lobed or angled, finely toothed
morphology.flowers: Upper axillary, involucel linear-spatulate, 5 red petals 2–3.5 cm rolled/contorted into tube; ten stigma/style branches from five carpels
morphology.fruit: Five indehiscent red fleshy berry-like carpels

records.diagnostic: Tubular-looking tightly rolled petals with projecting ten-branched style/stigma and fleshy red segmented fruit
holds: Flora treats as variety; some modern references split M. drummondii: keep source-specific rank
Old county citations include cultivated escape; county-native range needs BONAP

records.source: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology.habit: Shrub or partially herbaceous plant around (1.5–)2 m, largely hairless or sparsely hairy
morphology.leaves: Ovate-lanceolate, five basal veins with apparent pinnate pattern; petioles to 12 mm
morphology.flowers: No involucel, five pointed calyx lobes, five stamens and thin styles
morphology.habitat: Sandy or rocky disturbed ground, southern Texas; landscape weed escape farther north

records.diagnostic: Winged star-shaped five-celled capsule, unlike Sida schizocarps; family now broad Malvaceae, previously Sterculiaceae
holds: Original flora says native southern half of Texas but northern finds introduced with sod; BONAP target area not established

morphology.habit: Woody-based herb/subshrub of central, south and southwestern Texas
morphology.leaves: Alternate, often small and narrow, details in full FNA account pending
morphology.flowers: Malvaceous 5-petaled flowers; precise petal dimensions not asserted without account
morphology.fruit: Schizocarp of mericarps; number and surface details pending full FNA text
morphology.habitat: Scattered dry sites, Central Texas and southern Texas noted by FNA

records.diagnostic: Modern Meximalva vs Sida filipes nomenclatural crosswalk verified; no premature photo-level distinguishing traits

morphology.leaves: Orbicular-ovate, palmately 3–5 lobed, toothed, up to 6 × 4 cm
morphology.flowers: Solitary axillary, petals salmon to purplish-red, 4–6 mm

records.flora_name: Hibiscus coccineus Walter (modern Flora of North America treatment)
records.source: Flora of North America / Kew POWO taxonomic crosswalk

morphology.habit: Tall perennial wetland mallow of eastern and southeastern United States; Texas local occurrence must be checked
morphology.leaves: Deeply palmately 3–5 lobed, 10–19 × 13–25 cm, narrow lanceolate lobes with scattered serrations, glabrous
morphology.flowers: Bright red separated five petals (6–)7.5–10 × 2.5–5.5 cm, staminal column 6.5–7 cm, exserted
morphology.fruit: Glabrous ovoid to globose capsule 2.8–3.5 cm
morphology.habitat: Wet habitats including swamps and freshwater shorelines

records.diagnostic: Long narrow leaf lobes and very open red star-like corolla with extremely protruding staminal column; not rolled Turk's-cap
holds: New combination Muenchhusia adopted by Kew; record original Hibiscus for source search
